title: Completed sharp chart at a single log regular point
statement:
Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ be its strict local ring [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Set $P=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$, $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, and let $I\subset A$ be generated by the structural images of nonunit log sections. Assume only at this point that $A/I$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] and
$$\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}P^{\rm gp}.$$
Then $A$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $P$ is a sharp fs monoid (its only invertible element is $0$). There is an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods, def-weil-etale-morphism] and a chart $a:P\to M|_W$ inducing the prescribed identification $P\cong\overline M_{\bar x}$. Its pullback is a chart of the pullback log structure on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. For some integer $n\ge0$, the maximal-ideal completion $\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is a nonzero Noetherian local ring with a chart-compatible isomorphism
$$\widehat A\cong B_k(P,n)\quad\text{if }A\text{ contains a field},$$
or
$$\widehat A\cong B_C(P,n)/(\theta)\quad\text{otherwise},\qquad
\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n).$$
Here in the latter case $k$ has prime characteristic $p$ and $C$ is a Cohen ring for $k$, with uniformizer $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. For a local coefficient ring $L$,
$$B_L(P,n)=\varprojlim_N L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)^N,$$
where $L[P]$ has $L$-basis $z^q$ and $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. The isomorphisms take the image of $\alpha(a(q))$ to the class of $z^q$. No log regularity away from $\bar x$ and no excellence hypothesis are assumed. Dimension and rank have the meanings of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70, whose hypothesis is explicitly log regularity at x, not global log regularity; VI 1.1--1.2 for the chart and strict-local conventions. Kato 1994, Theorem 3.2, cited there, is not locally available.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing the image $x$ of $\bar x$, with $R$ Noetherian, using local Noetherianity. Restricting pointed neighbourhoods to the inverse image of $U$ is cofinal: each neighbourhood is refined by its inverse image of $U$, which still contains its marked geometric point. The ordinary local ring is $R_{\mathfrak q_x}$ by the affine stalk-localization statement, hence is Noetherian by localization permanence. The geometric strict-henselization presentation identifies $A$ as a strict henselization of such a local ring. Therefore strict-henselization Noetherianity makes $A$ Noetherian. The strict-local-structure statement makes $A$ a nonzero local ring; equivalently its geometric residue map takes $1$ to $1$ in a field.

Choose an fs chart $c:Q\to M$ near $\bar x$ from the definition of fs. Put $F=(\alpha c)^{-1}(A^\times)$ and $Q_F=Q-F$ inside $Q^{\rm gp}$. The face-localized chart lemma says that $F$ is a face, identifies $M_{\bar x}$ with $Q_F\oplus_{F^{\rm gp}}A^\times$, and canonically identifies $Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$ with the prescribed $P=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$. Thus we keep the given identification of the characteristic, rather than replacing it by an unspecified isomorphic monoid.

source.place: VI 1.1, 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp.69,70,75; the initial sharp-chart construction.

proof.text: Face sharpening applied to $Q,F$ says that $Q_F$ is fs integral with units $F^{\rm gp}$, that $P=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$ is sharp fs, and that $P^{\rm gp}$ is free of finite rank. Apply the integral-monoid free-sharpening splitting to $Q_F$. It gives a section $s:P\to Q_F$ and an isomorphism $P\oplus F^{\rm gp}\to Q_F$, $(q,f)\mapsto s(q)+f$. Here torsion in the units is allowed. With $\lambda:Q_F\to M_{\bar x}$ from step 2, the conditional conclusion of the face-localized chart lemma gives $h=\lambda s$ and $P\oplus A^\times\simeq M_{\bar x}$. The inverse image of ring units under $\alpha h$ is $\{0\}$, and the induced characteristic map is exactly the specified one.

source.place: VI 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp.70,75; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp.98--99.

proof.text: The fine-log stalk-chart spreading statement applies to $h$: $P$ is finitely generated integral, and the associated-log-stalk map is the isomorphism obtained in step 3. It supplies an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $W$ and a chart $a:P\to M|_W$ with exactly this germ. To check the pullback assertion, use the universal property of integral chart logification for the scheme map $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$. For every log structure $K$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, maps from $v^{-1}M|_W$ to $K$ compatible with structural maps correspond to maps $P\to\Gamma(K)$ lying over the pulled-back structural functions. Applying the same statement with the identity map on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ identifies the latter maps with maps from the logification of $P\to A$ to $K$. These bijections preserve the maps on $P$, so the universal property of pullback identifies the pulled-back log structure with this logification. Hence the pulled-back $a$ is a chart.

source.place: VI 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp.69,75; chart spreading and the associated-log universal property (agent detail).

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70; coefficient and surjection construction, Stacks Tag 032A, algebra-theorem-cohen-structure-theorem.

proof.text: Suppose $A$ contains a field, so $L=k$. Set $D=k[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$. The power-series regularity statement makes $D$ a nonzero complete regular Noetherian local ring of dimension $n$. The polynomial/power-series monoid-completion comparison identifies $B_k(P,n)$ with the completion of $D[P]$ at $(\mathfrak m_D,z^q:q\ne0)$, fixing each monomial. Apply formal-monoid-ring dimension to this $D$ and the sharp fs monoid $P$. Thus $B_k(P,n)$ is a Noetherian local integral domain of dimension $n+r$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i), printed p.70; monoid-model dimension input; Stacks Tags 032C (algebra-remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), 00KQ (algebra-proposition-dimension), 07NV (more-algebra-lemma-completion-dimension).

proof.text: Let $K=\ker\phi$ in the field case. If $K\ne0$, choose a chain of length $n+r$ in $S$, which exists because its dimension is the finite integer $n+r$. Inverse images under the surjection $\phi$ are a strictly increasing chain of prime ideals in $B_k(P,n)$: primality follows by applying $\phi$ to products, and strictness follows by lifting an element of each successive difference. Every prime of this chain contains nonzero $K$, so prepending the prime $(0)$ of the domain makes a chain of length $n+r+1$. This contradicts step 6. Therefore $K=0$, and the surjective $\phi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: VI 1.6(i), printed p.70, agent-supplied elementary finite-dimension kernel argument; Stacks Tag 00KE, algebra-definition-Krull.

proof.text: Suppose $A$ contains no field. Step 5 supplies $C$, a prime $p$, $\dim S=n+r$ and $\phi(J)=\mathfrak m_S$. Since $p$ maps into $\mathfrak m_S$, choose $j\in J$ with $\phi(j)=\phi(p)$. Apply the Cohen-monoid surjection principal-kernel statement with this $C,P,n,S,\phi$. Its hypotheses require only the sharp fs monoid, the nonzero Noetherian local target, the stated dimension and maximal-ideal image; all were established in steps 3 and 5. It yields $\ker\phi=(\theta)$ for $\theta=p-j$, with $\theta-p\in J$, and an isomorphism $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)\simeq S$ carrying every monomial class to its specified image.

source.place: VI 1.6(ii), printed p.70; mixed-characteristic principal-kernel argument.

proof.text: Invert the isomorphism of step 7 or step 8. In either case the resulting map from $\widehat A$ sends the completion image of $\alpha(a(q))$ to the class of $z^q$, since that is the defining formula for $\phi$. The chart remains the affine pointed chart from step 4, with its prescribed characteristic map and its pullback chart. No step used log regularity at another point or excellence. The empty cases are included: $P=0$ gives $I=0$ and the usual regular local completion; $n=0$ gives $\mathfrak m_A=I$. If both vanish then $A$ is a field, $S=k$, and $B_k(0,0)=k$. The nonzero and local assertions for $A$ and $S$ were established in steps 1 and 5.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70, assembly and degenerate cases.
